result.summary: The layout is generally coherent, but the horizontal carousels clip cards at the right edge, the active 'Pizza' filter doesn't appear to affect the listings, and the favorite icon styling is inconsistent between cards.

issues.description: The 'Pizza' category chip is shown as selected (black/active), yet the listings below are unfiltered — poké, burgers, ramen and generic 'Fastest near you'/'Popular right now' sections are displayed with no pizza-specific results at the top.
issues.suggestion: Either apply the selected category filter to the content sections or reset the chip to 'All' when no filter is applied.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' carousel the third card ('Trattoria Piccol…') is hard-clipped by the screen edge, cutting both the image and the '€1.90 delivery' label mid-text with no trailing gutter.
issues.suggestion: Add horizontal padding/peek so the next card is intentionally partially visible, and ensure card titles truncate with an ellipsis inside the card rather than being cut by the viewport.

issues.description: The category chip row is also clipped at the right edge, showing a sliver of an unnamed chip after 'Healthy', which looks like a rendering glitch rather than a scroll affordance.
issues.suggestion: Use consistent edge padding and a fade/gradient mask to signal horizontal scrollability.

issues.description: Favorite (heart) buttons are styled inconsistently: white circle with dark outline on the ramen card, but a dark/translucent circle on the pizza card below, reducing icon contrast.
issues.suggestion: Standardize the favorite button background and icon color across all restaurant cards, ensuring sufficient contrast over varied photography.

issues.description: The second 'Popular right now' card is cut off by the bottom tab bar with its title and metadata hidden, giving the impression of clipped content.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom content inset equal to the tab bar height so cards scroll fully clear of the navigation.

issues.description: The notification bell badge and 'See all' green links rely on color alone / small hit targets; the promo banner's secondary text also has lower contrast against the green fill.
issues.suggestion: Ensure link and badge states have text or icon cues plus at least 4.5:1 contrast, and use minimum 44x44pt tap targets.
